kitPage.faq1Q: How many photos can I put on the {kit} jersey?
kitPage.faq1A: One to three. They stack vertically inside the number, in the order you add them. Three photos give the richest result on a wide digit.
kitPage.faq2Q: Do my photos need a particular background?
kitPage.faq2A: No. Photos are used whole and clipped by the shape of the digit, so your background becomes part of the design. A bright, sharp photo with the subject centred works best.
kitPage.faq3Q: How long does it take and how do I pay?
kitPage.faq3A: Your order is recorded immediately with its preview. Payment is by bank transfer or finalised over WhatsApp: we confirm every order by hand before production starts.

gift.name: Gift for a football fan
gift.metaTitle: Gift for a football fan: the jersey with their own photos
gift.metaDescription: They already own every shirt their club makes. Not this one: their name, their number, and your photos inside the digits. Shipping across Europe and the USA.
gift.h1: A gift for the fan who already owns everything
gift.intro: The trouble with football fans is that they already have the home shirt, the away shirt and usually the third one too. One more just fills a shelf. This one is different: the number printed on the back is cut out of your photos — the stadium, the sofa, the nights that went to penalties.
gift.tip1Title: Start from their club, not yours
gift.tip1Body: A fan recognises a shirt instantly and spots a wrong shade just as fast. Pick their national side or their club from the catalogue: these are real product photos, so the colour is right.
gift.tip2Title: Three photos is the sweet spot
gift.tip2Body: Photos are stacked vertically inside the digits. Three works best: they stay readable and they tell a story. Choose images where faces are large — a wide landscape shot disappears inside the stroke of a number.
gift.tip3Body: Their lucky number, their favourite player's, the year of their first match at the ground. The name above can be a nickname rather than a surname — that is what raises a smile when the parcel is opened.
gift.faq1Q: What if I get the size wrong?
gift.faq1A: Sizes run from XS to XXL and follow classic football shirt cuts. If you are unsure, size up: a printed shirt is happily worn a little loose.
gift.faq2Q: Can I order without them knowing?
gift.faq2A: Yes, that is the usual case. You choose the shirt, the name, the number and the photos; we never contact them. Every order is confirmed by hand before it goes into production, which leaves time to fix a detail.

birthday.name: Birthday gift
birthday.metaTitle: Original birthday gift: the jersey numbered with their age
birthday.metaDescription: The number on the back is their age. Inside it, your photos from the year. A birthday present that looks like nothing else.
birthday.h1: The jersey whose number is their age
birthday.intro: Thirty years old, number 30. The idea fits in one line, and that is what makes it work: the digit reads from across the room, and up close you discover it is filled with photographs — this year's trip, this year's friends. The gift gets looked at twice.
birthday.tip1Body: Anything from 1 to 99 works. A single digit — 7, 9 — leaves more room for the photos than a two-digit number, where each digit gets its own cut-out.
birthday.tip2Title: Photos from this year, not the archive
birthday.tip2Body: The shirt marks one specific year. Pick three photos from the last twelve months rather than a greatest-hits selection: that is what dates the gift and gives it its value ten years from now.
birthday.tip3Body: The preview is instant, but printing and shipping take a few days. Two weeks of margin means you can approve the result calmly instead of ordering in a panic the night before.
birthday.faq1Q: Can I use a two-digit number?
birthday.faq1A: Yes, up to 99. Each digit is cut out separately and gets its share of the photos: the result stays readable, each image simply covers a smaller area.
birthday.faq2Q: How long before the date should I order?
birthday.faq2A: Allow around ten days from order to delivery, shipping included. We confirm every order by hand: if the date is tight, say so when you validate.

couple.name: Gift for a couple
couple.metaTitle: Gift for a couple: two matching jerseys with your photos
couple.metaDescription: Two shirts, the same photos, two numbers that answer each other. A couple's gift idea for an anniversary or Valentine's Day.
couple.h1: Two jerseys telling the same story
couple.intro: A personalised shirt works well on its own; as a pair it becomes a statement. Both carry the same photos inside the number, but each has its own: the day and the month you met — two numbers that mean nothing to anyone else.
couple.tip1Title: Two numbers that answer each other
couple.tip1Body: The day on one, the month on the other. Or both your ages, or 0 and 1. It works because neither shirt makes sense alone: side by side, they spell a date.
couple.tip2Body: Use exactly the same selection on both orders. Since photos are cropped identically inside each digit, the two backs echo each other instead of looking mismatched.
couple.tip3Body: Nothing says you must pick the same shirt. A home kit and its away version — same team, two shades — make a coherent pair without being a uniform. It usually photographs better.
couple.faq1Q: Do I need to place two orders?
couple.faq1A: Yes, one per shirt: each order carries its own size, name and number. Nothing special to flag — just reuse the same photo selection at step 4.
couple.faq2Q: Can I put two first names on one shirt?
couple.faq2A: The printed name takes up to 15 characters including spaces, so "ANNA & LUC" fits. Beyond that, letters condense horizontally the way real printing does: still readable, just tighter.

team.name: Team or club
team.metaTitle: Custom jerseys for an amateur team or club
team.metaDescription: A set of shirts on the same kit, each with its own name, number and photos. For an amateur side, a corporate tournament or an end-of-season gift.
team.h1: A set of jerseys for the whole squad
team.intro: Amateur sides usually order identical shirts, printed in a rush. Here everyone keeps the same kit — so the same look on the pitch — but the back belongs to each player: their name, their number, and their photos inside the digits. It is the end-of-season gift that does not end up at the bottom of a kit bag.
team.tip1Body: Agree the shirt and the finish level before anyone orders, and tell the group. Mixed finishes show: print sizes differ from one level to the next.
team.tip2Body: Each player places their own with their size, name, number and photos. It beats filling in a spreadsheet, and nobody guesses someone else's size.
team.tip3Body: Nothing stops two players picking 10. Circulate the list of taken numbers before the group orders: it is the one thing that cannot be fixed afterwards.
team.faq1A: Listed prices are the same whatever the quantity. For a large order, write to us before placing it: we confirm every order by hand and can discuss it then.
team.faq2Q: Can everyone share the same artwork?
team.faq2A: Yes. If the group uses the same photos — the season's, for instance — only the name and number change from shirt to shirt. Seen from behind, the set stays very consistent.

family.name: Family photo
family.metaTitle: Custom family jerseys with your own photos
family.metaDescription: The same family photos inside everyone's number, from XS to XXL. For a family reunion, a first match, or the Christmas photo.
family.h1: The same photos, one jersey each
family.intro: A family photo ends up in a frame; a jersey gets worn. By reusing the same photo selection on every order, the whole family ends up with the same artwork on the back — each with their own first name and number. XS for the youngest, XXL for the uncle who commentates every match.
family.tip1Body: The digits slice photos into vertical bands, so a wide landscape gets lost. Favour portraits or tight crops shot in daylight. It is the single criterion that really changes the result.
family.tip2Title: The same three photos for everyone
family.tip2Body: Keep the selection identical from one order to the next: that is what makes it a set. Because photos are cropped the same way inside each digit, the backs match even with different numbers.
family.tip3Body: Everyone's age, the children's birth years, or simply 1, 2, 3 and 4 in order of arrival. Lined up in a group photo they form a caption nobody needs to explain.
family.faq1A: The catalogue runs XS to XXL in adult cuts. XS suits a teenager; on a younger child it will be roomy — many families accept that, since a slightly big shirt lasts for years.
family.faq2Q: Can the family mix several teams?
family.faq2A: Nothing stops you, each order stands alone. In a group photo a shared kit reads stronger; different kits tell another story — and often that is exactly the point.
